COMMON GROUND — ALL FOUR BOARDS, ALL FOUR EMITTERS AND THE PACK
One star point. A low-side switch puts motor return current through the ground net, so run it in thick wire and keep it off the signal grounds. See SCHEMA_POWER.svg.
1. One PN2222A per motor, not per pair. At 250 mA each you have 2× margin on the 600 mA
rating; a whole pair on one device sits right at the limit and will not survive.
2. The flyback diode is mandatory. Without it the motor's collapsing field puts a spike
far above the 2222's 40 V V(CEO) on the collector, and kills it on the first switch-off.
3. A STALLED MOTOR KILLS THE TRANSISTOR. At 0.8 A it falls out of saturation and burns
~2.4 W in a TO-92 rated 0.6 W. Never let the car push against something — see note 6.
4. The 10 kΩ base pull-down is what makes the safe state real: it holds the base at 0 V
while the Arduino is in reset, so the motors cannot run before the sketch starts.
5. Only P3_27 / P3_28 are 5 V tolerant on the MCX. Both Arduino TX lines reach it through
a 1 kΩ / 2 kΩ divider. TX and RX cross: an MCX TX pin always lands on an Arduino D4.
6. With no encoders you cannot detect a stall directly. Three cheap substitutes: cap the
duty, cut the motors if the ultrasonic range stops changing while you are commanding
forward, and watch the accelerometer — a car that is really moving vibrates.
7. No reverse. One switch conducts one way, so the car drives forward and turns; it
cannot back out of a dead end. Plan the course, and pivot rather than reverse.
8. Two separate I²C buses. LPI2C0 is 3.3 V (ESP32 + IMU). The LCD is on ACT's own 5 V bus.
9. Servo V+ comes from the pack, never from an Arduino 5 V pin. ESP32 GPIO6–11 are wired
to its flash; GPIO0 is a strapping pin, so unplug the camera to flash the board.
10. Wheels off the floor until you have watched duty 0 and a pulled link both stop them.
